task.name: A provider-reported dated model version does not resolve, so evidence accrues under a key nothing can group by
task.story_text:
## Observed

The model version a provider actually reports does not resolve to a catalog identity, so evidence
recorded against it cannot be grouped by the thing it identifies.

Anthropic returns dated version strings in billed components — `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` appears
in `cost.agents[].ledger.billed_components[].identity`. That string does not resolve:

```
claude-haiku-4-5            -> anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5/cli
claude-haiku-4-5-20251001   -> UNRESOLVED
claude-sonnet-5             -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-5/cli
claude-sonnet-5-20250101    -> UNRESOLVED
claude-opus-4-8             -> UNRESOLVED
```

The undated form of the same model resolves; adding the date suffix the provider actually uses
makes it fail. Resolution falls back to recording the raw string with status `unresolved`, which is
truthful, and the evidence then accumulates under a key nothing else can match.

This lands directly on what versioned identity was introduced to achieve. Recording which concrete
version an alias served is only useful if that recorded version can be grouped, compared against
its siblings, or offered as an alternative — all of which require it to resolve. The record
improved; what can be done with it did not.

## Expected

An identity a provider reports is the most authoritative statement available about what ran, and it
is the form the system will encounter most often, since it is what the provider chooses to send.
Resolution that succeeds on a hand-written shorthand and fails on the provider's own spelling is
inverted with respect to which one matters.

A version and its dated release are the same model at a level of precision the provider added, not
two different subjects. Whatever identity they resolve to should reflect that, so observations of
one are observations of the other unless something deliberately distinguishes them.

Where an identity genuinely cannot be resolved, recording it verbatim and marking it unresolved is
the right behaviour and should stay. What should not happen is that the ordinary case — a provider
naming its own model in its own format — routinely takes that path, because a status meant to mark
the exceptional then describes the common case and stops carrying information.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** billed components carrying provider-reported dated version strings are
  recorded with resolution `unresolved`, while the same models' undated forms resolve.
- **Evidence:** `coordinator/agent_identity.py:56` `_canonicalize` returns
  `(raw, RESOLUTION_UNRESOLVED)` when `model_profiles.canonical_id_for_legacy_key` yields nothing.
  Direct calls to that function resolve `claude-haiku-4-5`, `claude-sonnet-5` and `claude-opus-5`,
  and fail on `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, `claude-sonnet-5-20250101` and `claude-opus-4-8`.
  `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` appears in current audit records as a billed component.
- **Ruled out:** not the alias-versus-version recording introduced for routing candidates. That
  works: `sonnet` and `claude-sonnet-5` appear at identical run counts, both canonical, which is
  the alias and its served version being recorded as intended.
- **Ruled out:** not stale records. Undated shorthands that appeared unresolved in records written
  before the shipped catalog landed now resolve under current code; the dated forms still do not.
- **Ruled out:** not a transport-hint problem. The failures reproduce with no hint and with both
  cli and api hints supplied.
- **Confirmed cause:** the legacy-key resolution path matches undated model spellings and has no
  handling for the dated release suffix providers append, so provider-reported identities fall
  through to the unresolved fallback.
- **Affected code path:** `model_profiles.canonical_id_for_legacy_key` and the canonicalization in
  `coordinator.agent_identity` that consumes it.
- **Fix-success criterion:** an identity as the provider reports it resolves to the same catalog
  identity as the corresponding undated form, so observations recorded under either are grouped
  together. An identity that genuinely corresponds to nothing in the catalog is still recorded
  verbatim and marked unresolved.

handoff.summary: canonical_id_for_legacy_key now normalizes a provider-appended release date before giving up. The existing resolution rules (2-5) were extracted verbatim into a _resolve_canonical_key helper; the public function calls it on the exact spelling first, and only if that yields nothing retries once on the date-stripped spelling. _strip_release_date matches a trailing -YYYYMMDD or -YYYY-MM-DD, pinned to a 20xx year with month 01-12 and day 01-31, optionally ahead of a -cli/-api transport suffix which is preserved. Because normalization only ever removes precision and never substitutes a different subject, a version with no catalog entry (claude-opus-4-8-20260101) stays unresolved, transport-hint ambiguity rules still apply to the stripped form, and the #2226 refusal to fold a concrete version onto its family shorthand is untouched (a version segment like -4-6 cannot match the date pattern). All consumers - agent_identity._canonicalize, the audit ledger writer, alias-drift, and the profiles migration - resolve through this one function, so they pick the fix up without change.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An identity as the provider reports it resolves to the same catalog identity as the corresponding undated form, so observations recorded under either are grouped together.
acceptance_criteria.notes: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 -> anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5/cli, claude-sonnet-5-20250101 -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-5/cli, claude-opus-5-20250101 -> anthropic/claude-opus-5/cli, each identical to its undated form. Pinned by TestDatedVersionResolvesLikeItsUndatedForm and by a seam test that writes a dated billed_component through audit_render._agent_entry and reads it back through entry_identity_ledger, asserting the component groups under the same key as the invocation's resolved identity.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An identity that genuinely corresponds to nothing in the catalog is still recorded verbatim and marked unresolved.
acceptance_criteria.notes: claude-opus-4-8 and claude-opus-4-8-20260101 both stay None/unresolved; an unknown spelling round-trips verbatim through canonicalize_identity with RESOLUTION_UNRESOLVED. Pinned by TestGenuinelyUnknownIdentitiesStayUnresolved.

handoff.story_deviations: Spec's Expected section ('a version and its dated release are the same model') was implemented narrowly, as the preflight warning recommended: only a provider date suffix on an already-concrete version is normalized. It does not reintroduce family-shorthand/version folding, which model_profiles.py documents as a deliberate #2226 decision.

reviews.summary: The change resolves provider-reported dated model spellings through the existing canonical identity path while preserving unresolved handling for genuinely unknown models.
